  • Werkio

    I built Werkio, a full-stack web app for finding student jobs and academic roles, and developed its AI-assisted application workflows across a TypeScript browser extension, React frontend, and Spring Boot backend.

    The Copilot uses Gemini to map profile data to application forms and draft cover letters from approved facts and job context. I added structured JSON validation and evidence checks, with review steps for uncertain or sensitive fields. Users review the proposed changes and submit applications themselves.

    I implemented workflow state and error handling so the extension can explain failures and invalidate stale plans when the active page changes. Access checks, CSRF protection, and feature flags control when actions are available.

    I wrote Playwright end-to-end tests that load the browser extension against controlled application forms. They cover multi-step forms, sensitive fields, provider and network failures, preserving user edits, and manual submission. Backend unit, integration, and security tests cover the API and persistence boundaries; GitHub Actions runs the checks before integration.

    The platform uses PostgreSQL and Flyway behind a REST API, with Docker Compose and Caddy on AWS EC2. Job matching and email digests support the core job-search product.

    Visit Werkio.

    Highlights
    • Built Gemini-based form mapping and cover-letter drafting across a TypeScript browser extension, React frontend, and Spring Boot backend.
    • Added structured-output validation, evidence checks, and review steps for uncertain or sensitive fields. Users stay in control of form submission.
    • Wrote Playwright end-to-end tests for browser workflows and failure cases, plus backend integration and security tests.
  • CHECK24 MCP App

    I built this MCP app for the CHECK24 GenDev scholarship task. It gives ChatGPT one endpoint for tools across hotel, flight, package-holiday, and insurance services, using mock data and adapters.

    The TypeScript and Node.js proxy namespaces tools, validates inputs and declared outputs with AJV, and withholds tools that fail conformance checks. Scoped QA endpoints let each service be tested separately. A dashboard displays validation findings, call traces, durations, and errors.

    The project uses Express, the MCP SDK, Vitest, and Docker Compose.

    View the project on GitHub.

    Highlights
    • Built a TypeScript and Node.js proxy that combines four mock product services into one MCP endpoint, with namespaced tools and schema validation.
    • Added conformance checks, scoped QA endpoints, and a dashboard for tool errors and call traces.
